script: "Will Ferrell's man‑child routine ruined every movie—this is why I am done watching.". I watched Will Ferrell on the big screen for the first time in that over‑the‑top "Anchorman" scene where he's yelling, "I am the best!" (I know, right?) and I instantly thought, "Bruh, this is just the same loud, clueless kid on repeat." He jumps into every role with that same energy: loud, clueless, overconfident, trying to dominate the room like it's a game of "who can shout the loudest?" It's like every time he turns on the volume, the whole movie turns up to 11. I am not saying it's a bad thing—he can be a solid supporting dude, like in "Step Brothers" where he's the goofy sidekick. But when he's the lead, it's like watching someone mistake being the loudest person in the room for being the funniest. (Literally insane.) The yelling, the awkwardness, the random outbursts—they all blend into a single routine. It's exhausting, not funny, and it feels like a bad remix of the same beat. I'd rather see a character with depth, not just a caricature of a man‑child. And honestly, it's the audacity of it all that cracks me up—except when it doesn't. So yeah, I am better than that. I prefer comedy that actually moves the story, not just a loud, clueless character who thinks he's the center of the universe. (I know, right?)
